note.question: Does a more accurate influencer-marketer recommendation technology always increase platform revenue, and how should a platform adjust its commission when improved matching intensifies competition among influencers?
note.overview: Heterogeneous influencers simultaneously post take-it-or-leave-it endorsement prices, marketers choose among them or stay out, and the platform collects a commission. The paper derives a unique competitive market-clearing equilibrium and analyzes how matching accuracy changes entry, prices, competition, and platform revenue.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Given a public matching-accuracy level, the platform's AI recommends influencers to each marketer. Influencers simultaneously post take-it-or-leave-it endorsement prices. Marketers then choose whether to participate and, if so, buy at most one endorsement. Matched influencers produce sponsored content, converted revenue is realized, and the platform retains its commission share.

models.name: Commission-design extension
models.relation: This extension builds on Equilibrium influencer pricing and participation under platform-mediated marketer matching.
models.summary: In other words, δ ∈ [0,1] can be endogenously set by the platform. In this extended model, the market expansion effect now consists of two components: the first is proportional to the equilibrium price of the most niche influencers who participate, and the second that of the most general influencers who participate. When all influencers have the same number of followers, the niche influencers provide sufficiently high revenue to marketers if the matching accuracy is sufficiently high (λ > λ) that only influencers with a content broadness lower than a threshold (n < n) participate in equilibrium unlike in our baseline model.
